elements.element: Vendor provides transition assistance on expiry or termination
elements.evidence: "Upon expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason, TrueLink shall (a) ... provide reasonable transition assistance"

elements.element: Transition assistance available for up to 6 months
Return of Customer Data within 30 days of expiry or termination (deadline running from expiry/termination, not a later request)
elements.evidence: "within thirty (30) days of Client's request, return to Client all Client Content ..." — the deadline runs from a request, not from expiry or termination

elements.element: Return in a standard machine-readable format
elements.evidence: "in a commonly used, machine-readable format" — "commonly used" is substituted for the required "standard" format specification
"(c) thereafter delete such data and information from its systems and certify such deletion to Client in writing"

elements.element: Data export within 30 days (of expiry or termination)
elements.evidence: "within thirty (30) days of Client's request" — the 30-day export duty is conditioned on and measured from a Client request, so no mandatory post-termination export deadline exists

offending_extra_words: except to the extent retention is required by applicable law or by any System Agreement or Credit Repository Agreement
reasons: Locked target is preferred, but the 30-day data-return deadline runs from "Client's request" rather than from expiry or termination; a request condition must not swallow the mandatory post-termination return. Delete "of Client's request" and run the period from expiration or termination.
Transition assistance is also gated on "at Client's request"; combined with the request-based return, Vendor owes no unconditional exit duty, so even the fallback 30-day export is not secured.
Format is "commonly used, machine-readable" rather than the required standard machine-readable format; state "standard machine-readable format" expressly.

Minimality fails: the inserted carve-out "except to the extent retention is required by applicable law or by any System Agreement or Credit Repository Agreement" introduces a broad new exception to the deletion/certification duty beyond what completing the preferred level requires (a narrow legal-retention carve-out would suffice, if any).
Untouched Sections 13 and 14 terms remain effective and no undefined term or dangling mechanic is introduced, so intent is otherwise preserved.
